messages.subject: Re: Interpreting beta parameters
messages.subject_clean: Interpreting beta parameters
messages.body_plain:
'beta' parameters are the coefficients of the model that is actually fitted when 'secr' maximises the likelihood i.e. the actual parameters that are estimated. Estimates of 'real' parameters (.e.g, density) are obtained using the coefficients to form a 'linear predictor' and back-transforming from the 'link' scale. For constant models there is a 1:1 relation between beta parameters and real parameters, otherwise it's many:1. The beta/.real jargon comes from the MARK software, and the MARK gentle introduction (Cooch and White) is a good place to learn more. The parameters are a bit different, but the same principles apply.
Murray

I have ocelot (Leopardus pardalis) data from seven systematic camera trap surveys. These surveys were realized in 2004, 2006, 2008, 2010, 2014, 2016 and 2018. I am fitting openCR models to estimate mainly survival and growth rate, using JSSAsecrlCL model type.

Hi Marine
It may be that your data stray so far from the assumptions of the statistical methods that applying the methods can only be misleading. This is especially true of the targeted resighting of known leopards at known places: understandable behaviour of guides, but bad for the statistics. The accuracy of locations recorded after the drive wouldn't bother me so much - I assume the drivers know their routes. The models require reliable negative evidence (from sampling across potential habitat) as well as positive sightings.
Sorry to bring bad news!
Murray
